title: Generation and live imaging of tumors with specific genotypes in the living fly pupa
protocol: Cross male flies carrying UAS-transgene on the 3rd chromosome with virgin female flies with FRT site and tubGal80 on the 2nd chromosome.
Incubate for 30–45 minutes followed by 10–13 days to achieve positively marked tumors through selective breeding.
Identify progeny carrying transgenes of interest using genetic markers.
Cross male F1 progeny of correct genotype, identified by absence of short hairs (MKRS), with females of the specified genotype.
Incubate as required for each step to generate homozygous mutant tumors.
Collect approximately 20 virgin female flies of the stock w; FRT40a, tub-Gal80; MKRS / TM6b.
Verify that the collected females express both MKRS and TM6b genetic markers.
Collect males from the specific UAS-transgene stock located on the 3rd chromosome.
Place collected virgin females with selected males in a fresh vial of food.
Incubate at 25°C.
Flip parent flies to a fresh vial of food twice a week, maintaining old and new vials separately.
Do not let F1 progeny mix with parent flies.
Cross specific F1 progeny males carrying the FRT site, tubGal80 and UAS-transgene with virgin females carrying the lgl mutant allele, FRT site, Ubx-Flp, Pnr-Gal4 and UAS-GFP:moe.
Select approximately 5 TM6b positive males from the progeny of the first cross.
Discard female flies.
Screen male F1 progeny for tubby (short, fat body) and humeral (extra macrochaetes) genetic markers.
Discard MKRS positive flies as they do not have an identifiable phenotype at the pupal stage.
Optional: Move the first cross to 18°C once males have been selected and second cross has been carried out.
Collect approximately 20 virgin female flies of stock Ubx-Flp; FRT40a, lgl4/CyO-GFP; Pnr-Gal4, UAS-GFP:moe / TM6b.
Verify that the stock is expressing CyO-GFP.
Ensure flies have curly wings and ubiquitous GFP expression.
Place the collected males from step 5 with virgin flies in a fresh vial of food.
Cross the males from step 5 to virgin females with genotype: Ubx-Flp; FRT40a; Pnr-Gal4,UAS-GFP:moe / TM6b.
Cross female virgins from step 6 with males of genotype: w; FRT40a, tub-Gal80 for lgl4 mutant clones without the UAS-transgene.
Cross Ubx-Flp; FRT40a; Pnr-Gal4,UAS-GFP:moe / TM6b female virgins to w; FRT40a, tub-Gal80 males for wild type clones.
Incubate all crosses at 25°C.
Flip the parent flies to a fresh vial of food twice a week.
Keep both the old and new vials at 25°C.
Check the vials regularly for forming pupae.
Set at least two second crosses for each genotype.
Identify F2 pupae of interest every hour for 4–5 hours daily until target number is reached.
Screen the F2 vials and collect all TM6b negative pre-pupae at 0 h APF using a damp small brush.
Discard brown pupae or leave them attached to the sides of the vials.
Collect flies at the pre-pupal stage, designated as 0 h APF.
Discard TM6b positive pupae that are tubby and shorter than wild-type.
Discard Cyo-GFP pupae expressing ubiquitous GFP.
Discard pupae with fluorescent salivary glands due to lack of tub-Gal80 segregation.
Collect non-tubby, GFP-positive pupae only in small clones in the notum area.
Collect entirely non-fluorescent pupae for analysis.
Identify pupae carrying the TM6b balancer by their short tubby phenotype.
Place the identified pupa on a petri dish covered with tissue paper soaked in water.
Label the exact time the pupa was collected and its genotype.
Screen the collected pre-pupae for fluorescent markers.
Discard CyO-GFP positive flies.
Identify CyO-GFP negative flies possessing both the FRT site and lgl mutant allele.
Discard GFP positive salivary glands.
Locate salivary glands on the ventral side of the pupa.
Incubate pupae with correct markers at 29°C overnight.
Mount pupae from 12 h after puparium formation (APF).
Image pupae between 20–24 h APF for optimal tissue observation.
Assemble the slides for high resolution confocal imaging.
Use tungsten forceps to pull the pupal case away from the pupa body along red dashed lines, ensuring not to pierce the body of the pupa.
Uncover only the head and dorsal thorax region of the animal using forceps.
Mount a pupa on a microscope slide using double-sided sticky tape along the center of the slide.
Remove protective paper from the double-sided sticky tape to expose the adhesive side.
Assemble two stacks of 3-5 square coverslips, gluing them together with nail polish.
Glue one stack of square coverslips at the anterior end and another at the posterior end of the microscope slide using nail polish.
Place the pupa on top of the sticky tape in the center of the slide, ventral side down.
Wait approximately 10 minutes for the pupa to fully attach to the tape.
Carefully remove a small region of the pupal case with tungsten forceps to expose the notum.
Spread one side of a rectangular coverslip (22 × 50 mm) with a thin layer of 10S voltalef injection oil.
Place the covered coverslip on top of the pupa, oil side down.
Verify that the rectangular coverslip is touching the notum.
Adjust the bridge if necessary.
Add or remove square coverslips from either side of the stack as needed.
Fix the long coverslip to the adjusted square coverslip stacks using nail polish.
Maintain assembled slides in a humid environment until ready for imaging.
Set the confocal microscope to take optical slices every 1 μm from the cuticle to the basal lamina.
Image the entire dorsal thorax epithelial sheet at a resolution of 1024 × 1024 (375 × 375 μm).
Image the whole notum with a single z-stack for clones fitting one field of view.
Use two z-stacks if the clones are very large and do not fit one field of view.
Image at least 5 animals per genotype.
